title: finding(scripts/pm): `post-stamped` prescribes the `{{WAS:…}}` spelling that H56 then files as an ESTIMATED stamp — and renders it with no marker, so H56 cannot tell a true reading from a guess
body:
`post-stamped.mjs` and `check-half-states.mjs`'s H56 row are the same family and disagree about one
line. `post-stamped` tells a seat to spell a genuine older reading `{{WAS:…}}` in a subscript
reading-time line; it then renders that token as a **bare stamp with no marker**; H56 reads the bare
stamp, measures it against the comment's own `created_at`, and files the seat for an ESTIMATED
stamp — and its remedy is "post it through `post-stamped.mjs`", which is what produced the line.

Filed from the `domain:ui#2` seat at objectstack-ai/objectui (`session_018HrVaotisyhgmot9o2MLRq`).
`scripts/pm/**` is objectstack's surface, so the card lands here per the single-writer rule.
All readings taken 2026-09-19T09:38Z on `origin/main` unless a row says otherwise.

## The live instance

objectstack-ai/objectui#9925, comment `5740450852`. Its subscript reading-time line carries
`2026-09-19T07:58Z` — the moment the CI job log was actually read. The comment was written after the
diagnosis and stored at `2026-09-19T08:21:37Z`. H56 files it:

> a subscript reading-time line of comment `5740450852` states `2026-09-19T07:58Z`, and the platform
> stored that comment at 2026-09-19T08:21:37Z — 23 minute(s) apart, beyond the 15-minute tolerance …
> it was ESTIMATED … Remedy … post it through `scripts/pm/post-stamped.mjs`

⛔ It WAS posted through `post-stamped.mjs`. The stamp is not estimated; it is the true reading time
of the thing the paragraph reports, and the seat wrote it as `{{WAS:2026-09-19T07:58Z}}` precisely
because `post-stamped` demanded that spelling.

The same sweep filed **6** H56 rows on this board, so this is a class rather than one comment.

## The two rules, quoted from the tools themselves

`post-stamped.mjs`, the POSITIONAL refusal it hands a seat for a bare stamp in that position:

> a subscript reading-time line carries the bare stamp `…`. That position belongs to the writing act,
> so a stamp typed there is the act's own time written from memory — the defect this tool exists to
> make unspellable. Write `2026-09-19T09:38Z` there, or `{{WAS:…}}` if it is genuinely a reading of something
> else.

`check-half-states.mjs`, H56 (`H56_STAMP_TOLERANCE_MIN = 15`, `H56_READING_LINE_OPENER = /<sub>/`,
`h56EstimatedStamp`): a stamp in an opening line **or a `<sub>` reading-time line** that differs from
the `created_at`..`updated_at` window by more than 15 minutes is filed as estimated.

⇒ `post-stamped` **prescribes** exactly the artefact H56 **files**.

## Why H56 cannot tell them apart — measured, not inferred

`post-stamped.mjs`'s `substituteTokens` renders a quoted token as its payload and nothing else:

```js
const was = quotedHere.exec(rest);
if (was) {
  if (isQuoted) { verbatim += 1; out += was[0]; }
  else          { quoted += 1;   out += was[1]; }   // ← bare payload, no marker
  i = at + was[0].length;
  continue;
}
```

⇒ the posted text carries `2026-09-19T07:58Z` and carries **no trace** that the author declared it a
reading of something else. The intent is encoded at write time and erased at post time, so a reader
downstream — H56 included — has nothing to read it by. That is the whole defect: it is not that H56
judges wrongly given what it can see, it is that the pair destroys the evidence H56 would need.

⚠️ What would make this not be the finding: a marker surviving into the posted text. There is none —
the substitution above is the only quoted-token path, and its `else` branch writes `was[1]` bare.

## Two directions, ⛔ neither chosen here

Both are the skills seat's call; this card only names them.

1. **Make the declaration survive.** Render a quoted stamp in a form H56 can recognise as declared —
   e.g. a fixed prefix in the reading-time position — and have `h56EstimatedStamp` skip it. Costs a
   visible spelling change on every existing reading-time line, and the two tools then share one
   vocabulary instead of two.
2. **Narrow H56's positions.** Drop the `<sub>` reading-time line from H56's population and keep the
   opening line, on the ground that a subscript reading-time line is BY CONSTRUCTION a reading of
   something else and therefore has no reason to track the write clock. Cheaper, and it gives up the
   ability to catch a genuinely estimated stamp in that one position.

⚠️ ⛔ Do not resolve it by telling seats to stop using `{{WAS:…}}` in that position: `post-stamped`
refuses the alternative, so that direction leaves the line unspellable rather than fixed.

Dedupe words: `H56 estimated stamp WAS token` · `post-stamped quoted token marker` ·
`subscript reading-time line tolerance` · `h56EstimatedStamp false positive` ·
`substituteTokens quoted bare payload`
